801	the people of Israel, that they are not
802	with him. They are not playing the same tune as he is. He is
803	entirely "We are going up to the Land that HaShem told
804	us about," with great enthusiasm. But the people of Israel
805	doubt and are afraid, and say: "Let us send men
806	ahead of us to spy out the land and dig it up. We are
807	going into the unknown."
808	So Moshe Rabbeinu immediately understands that here he has
809	the role of the one who calms,
810	the national calmer. How will he calm them now? The
811	first thing is to give them confidence. That is what is called the
812	first,
813	simple tactic. They come and say to you, "We
814	want to send spies, we are afraid." Moshe Rabbeinu
815	surely thinks: what is the problem? What is expected to happen?
816	That Moshe Rabbeinu will show them such confidence that they
817	will drop the idea. He goes with the flow, they will go with the flow with him,
818	and they move on. "Time will do what reason cannot," as they say. But in this case it did not work.
819	They did not give up.
820	The people of Israel keep being pests, because they have
821	the Erev Rav, who sat there at the tail, and they
822	do not accept a refusal. They want to send
823	spies. And this is truly an expression of lack of trust in the Holy One,
824	Blessed Be He, because the Holy One, Blessed Be He, took them out of Egypt
825	and said, "I will bring you up to a good and broad land."
826	To come and say to the Holy One, Blessed Be He, "We do not rely on Your power to conquer the Land of Israel,
827	we want to send
828	spies" is worse than a joke. It is
829	something for which there is no greater disgrace than this.
830	Who has to be at the head of the mission? What would Moshe Rabbeinu
831	have to do? He cannot be,
832	he cannot be at the head of the delegation. Have you ever seen the head of an army
833	who goes to be a spy? There is no such thing.
834	Now, so what do we do? So Moshe
835	Rabbeinu understood what is hidden behind the words.
836	He said: they are afraid and do not believe
